acceptance_criteria: Holm-adjusted VIX CAR p-value below 0.05 (one-sided, negative direction)
Standardized mean VIX CAR at or below -0.3
spec.alternative_hypothesis: Mean CAR[0,+1] is negative for VIX (primary) and TYVIX and non-zero for SPX, DGS10 and BAA10Y, with the VIX standardized mean CAR at or below -0.3.
spec.benchmark: Constant-mean expected return: the mean observed change over each event's own estimation window [-60,-11], estimated separately per event and per leg
cost_assumptions: No cost gate applies: an event study measures announcement responses, not a forecast, and there is no trading rule to cost. A significant CAR is evidence about how markets respond to scheduled announcements, not a tradable edge.
spec.cost_model: No cost gate: an event study measures announcement responses, not a forecast; there is no trading rule to cost
exclusions: Unscheduled meetings, cancelled meetings, conference calls and notation votes are excluded (listed in the report).
FOMC minutes releases are not events in this study.
Events with an incomplete estimation window ([-60,-11]) or event window ([0,+1]) are excluded and counted.
Bars outside the sample (2003-01-02 to 2020-05-15) are out of sample for the main tests; the extended sample (non-TYVIX legs to 2026-11-16) is descriptive only.
The [-1,+1] window and the policy-cycle splits are descriptive only and are not in the test family.
fixed_parameters: event_source=federalreserve fomchistorical pages 2003-2020 and fomccalendars.htm 2021 onwards
statement_time=14:00 ET on the last meeting day
known_confounders: The DGS10 event-window move is only a proxy for the policy surprise, not the surprise itself: no free federal funds futures surprise series exists.
An event study measures announcement responses, not tradable alpha; a significant CAR is not a trading strategy.
Estimation windows may contain a prior meeting's event window (2 of 50 days when meetings are five weeks apart); the contamination is small and the simple [-60,-11] rule is kept as preregistered.
FRED publication lag is not modelled; available_at equals the close.
TYVIX was discontinued in May 2020; the main sample ends 2020-05-15 and excludes the post-2020 hiking cycle.
Other macro releases occasionally coincide with FOMC statement days; they are not excluded — the event window is defined by the FOMC calendar only.
The calendar is extracted from the Fed's own pages, not rule-constructed; the residual risk is a parsing error, guarded by the per-year count checks and the cross-checks.
spec.mechanism: Scheduled announcements resolve policy uncertainty: implied volatility should fall after the statement as uncertainty is removed (the post-announcement volatility drop), while the rates leg reprices on the policy news and the repricing transmits to equities and credit. The DGS10 event-window move is only a proxy for the policy surprise, not the surprise itself: there is no free federal funds futures surprise series (a Kuttner-style surprise needs futures data). This study tests the cross-sectional association between the rates leg and the other legs, not a causal surprise effect.
spec.missing_data_policy: No forward filling; drop incomplete synchronized rows and report the dropped count. Events whose t=0 is absent from the panel or whose estimation or event window does not fit inside the panel are excluded and counted.
model_definition: Constant-mean event study via the repo event_study() estimator (estimation window [-60,-11], event window [0,+1], overlap-cluster inference)
One-sided p-values for the volatility legs derived from the estimator z-statistic as Phi(z) for the 'less than' direction; two-sided p-values for SPX, DGS10 and BAA10Y
Holm family of 5 tests (a VIX, b SPX, c DGS10, d BAA10Y, e TYVIX); effect size is the standardized mean CAR
Descriptive [-1,+1] window, descriptive extended sample (non-TYVIX legs to 2026-11-16) and descriptive policy-cycle splits (hiking / cutting / unchanged, no p-values)
spec.multiple_testing_family: FOMC event-window CARs (5 tests: a VIX CAR[0,+1] < 0, b SPX CAR[0,+1] != 0, c DGS10 CAR[0,+1] != 0, d BAA10Y CAR[0,+1] != 0, e TYVIX CAR[0,+1] < 0)
spec.null_hypothesis: Mean CAR[0,+1] around scheduled FOMC statement days is zero on every leg; announcement days are indistinguishable from ordinary days after the constant-mean benchmark.
spec.primary_metric: Standardized mean VIX CAR[0,+1] (mean CAR divided by the cross-event standard deviation of CARs)
rejection_criteria: Holm-adjusted VIX CAR p-value at or above 0.05 (one-sided, negative direction)
spec.research_question: Do scheduled FOMC statement days produce significant cumulative abnormal returns in the [0,+1] event window across the rates (DGS10), credit (BAA10Y spread), equity (SPX) and volatility (VIX, TYVIX) legs?
spec.target_definition: Per-leg cumulative abnormal return over the [0,+1] event window around scheduled FOMC statement days (VIX and TYVIX log changes, SPX log return, DGS10 and BAA10Y level changes in basis points)
spec.title: FOMC statements move rates, credit, equity and volatility
